records.title: Power Convertible Top Hydraulic System Failure
records.description: The hydraulic power convertible top system develops leaks in the hydraulic cylinders, lines, and pump motor. The system is complex with multiple actuators for the folding hardtop/softtop mechanism. Hydraulic fluid leaks onto the trunk carpet and the top may stop mid-cycle, leaving it partially open.
records.solution: Inspect all hydraulic cylinders and lines for leaks. Replace worn hydraulic cylinders and rebuild the hydraulic pump. Use the correct hydraulic fluid — never substitute brake fluid or ATF. The hydraulic reservoir is in the trunk area. Lubricate all pivot points during service. A convertible top specialist is recommended for this complex mechanism.
symptoms: Motor runs but top does not move

records.title: Coolant Crossover Pipe and Thermostat Housing Leak
records.description: The Catera 3.0L V6 coolant crossover pipe and plastic thermostat housing develop cracks and leaks. The plastic components become brittle with heat cycling and fail, causing coolant loss and overheating that can warp the aluminum cylinder heads.
records.solution: Replace the thermostat housing and coolant crossover pipe. Upgrade to aluminum aftermarket components if available. Replace the thermostat at the same time. Flush the cooling system with fresh coolant.

records.title: 3.0L V6 Coolant Leak and Overheating
records.description: The Catera 3.0L V6 develops multiple coolant leaks from the water pump, thermostat housing, and hose connections. Overheating from these leaks can warp cylinder heads.
records.solution: Pressure-test the cooling system and inspect the water pump, thermostat housing/coolant bridge, radiator end tanks, and all upper/lower hose connections for seepage or crusted coolant residue; on the Catera’s 3.0L V6, leaks commonly come from the water pump and plastic housing seals. Replace the failed components with updated gaskets/O-rings, install a new thermostat while the system is apart, and refill/bleed with the correct Dex-Cool coolant mixture to prevent air pockets that can trigger overheating. If the engine has overheated, check for combustion gases in the coolant and verify cylinder head flatness before returning it to service, since warped heads are a known risk. Typical repair cost ranges from about $400-$900 for hoses/thermostat housing repairs and $700-$1,300 if the water pump and related seals are replaced.

records.title: 3.0L V6 Timing Belt Failure

records.title: 4L30-E Automatic Transmission Harsh Shifts and Slipping
records.description: The GM 4L30-E automatic transmission develops harsh 1-2 and 2-3 shifts, slipping, and delayed engagement. The valve body wears internally and the torque converter clutch material contaminates the fluid. Neglected fluid changes accelerate the problems significantly.
records.solution: Service the transmission with a fluid and filter change first. If shifting does not improve, a valve body rebuild or replacement is needed. In severe cases, a transmission rebuild or replacement is the only option. Use Dexron III fluid as specified. Regular 30,000-mile fluid changes prevent most issues.

records.title: Power Window Regulator Cable Failure

records.solution: Replace the window regulator assembly. Aftermarket units are available but verify fitment as the Catera uses Opel-specific parts. Lubricate the window channels with dry silicone spray during installation. Have spare door panel clips on hand as they break during removal.
symptoms: Motor runs but window does not move

records.title: 12V Auxiliary Battery Drain on Ultium Platform
records.description: The Celestiq shares the GM Ultium platform with the Lyriq and Blazer EV, and inherits the 12V auxiliary battery drain issue common to these vehicles. The vehicle electronics draw power from the 12V battery even when parked, and the high-voltage system may not always recharge it properly. If the 12V battery drains below a critical threshold, the vehicle may fail to start or exhibit various electronic malfunctions. This is exacerbated by the Celestiq's extensive electronic systems including the 55-inch display and advanced lighting.
records.solution: Keep the vehicle plugged in when parked for extended periods to allow the HV system to maintain the 12V battery. If the 12V battery dies, use the designated jump-start terminals under the hood. Ensure the latest software update is installed as GM has released calibration fixes. Consider a trickle charger for long-term storage.
symptoms: Vehicle fails to power on after sitting for several days
Warning messages about low 12V battery on display
Electronic systems behaving erratically on startup
Key fob unable to communicate with vehicle
Delayed response when pressing start button

records.title: 10L80 10-Speed Torque Converter Clutch (TCC) Shudder at Light Throttle
records.description: The CT5 pairs both its 2.0L turbo and 3.0L twin-turbo engines with a GM 10-speed automatic (10L80/10L90), which can develop a torque converter clutch (TCC) shudder felt as a vibration or 'rumble-strip' shake, typically at light throttle and steady cruise (roughly 25-55 mph) when the converter clutch is applying. The accepted root cause is TCC friction-material shedding and fluid contamination degrading TCC apply. GM issued TSB 22-NA-080 covering 10L80/10L90 TCC shudder (added July 2022, later revised to add newer model years). This is distinct from the 10L80/10L90 control-valve-wear recall and from harsh-shift/solenoid codes. Verified: TSB 22-NA-080 exists and covers this transmission family; CT5 use of the 10-speed with both engines is confirmed; CT5/V-Series owner shudder reports are corroborated on forums.
records.solution: Per TSB 22-NA-080, the fix is a Transmission Control Module (TCM) recalibration combined with a complete transmission fluid exchange to the specified Mobil 1 Synthetic LV ATF HP (GM PN 19417577). If shudder persists after the fluid/recalibration service (indicating advanced clutch-material contamination), the torque converter and a full fluid flush/replacement are required.
symptoms: Vibration or shudder at light throttle / steady cruise
'Rumble-strip' shake felt through the vehicle around 25-55 mph
Shudder most noticeable when torque converter clutch engages
Momentary shake that comes and goes under light load

records.title: 10L80 Harsh Shifts and Check Engine Light with DTC P2812 or P2814 (Line Pressure Solenoid)
records.description: Owners of 2020-2021 Cadillac CT5 and CT5-V models equipped with the GM Hydra-Matic 10L80 10-speed automatic report harsh, abrupt shifts accompanied by an illuminated check engine light. GM Preliminary Information bulletin PIP5799 documents an electrical fault in Transmission Control Solenoid Valve 7 (the line pressure solenoid) that stores DTC P2812 or P2814 in the TCM. Separately, NHTSA Safety Recall N242480630 (NHTSA 25V148) covers TCM monitoring software for a related transmission control valve wear condition that, in rare cases, can cause momentary wheel lock-up. A related Special Coverage bulletin (N242480631) extends warranty for the P0747 control-valve condition to 15 years / 150,000 miles. Note: the 2020-2021 CT5 does not include the CT5-V Blackwing (introduced for MY2022 with the 10L90), which is NOT part of this recall population.
records.solution: Scan the TCM; if P2812 or P2814 is set, follow SI diagnostics for the line pressure solenoid circuit. PIP5799 directs that, if no other root cause is found, the valve body is replaced. Also verify GM Safety Recall N242480630 (TCM monitoring software for wheel lock-up risk) has been performed; owner letters were mailed April 7, 2025. If P0747 sets after the TCM update, the control valve body replacement is covered under Special Coverage N242480631 for 15 years / 150,000 miles.
symptoms: Reduced engine performance / Reduced Propulsion message
Possible momentary wheel lock-up (subject of recall N242480630)

records.title: 2.0L Turbo (LSY) Excessive Oil Consumption and PCV System Failure
records.description: Owners of four-cylinder CT5 550T (and CT4-shared LSY platform) models report higher-than-expected oil consumption, often exceeding GM's 'acceptable' threshold of one quart per ~2,000 miles. The valve-cover-integrated PCV system is a frequent contributor, and on worse cases worn piston rings or turbo seals allow oil into the combustion chamber. Symptoms commonly appear between 40,000 and 80,000 miles and are accompanied by low-oil warnings between changes, a lit check-engine light, and sometimes boost/lean codes. The PCV diaphragm is built into the valve cover, so a failed PCV requires valve-cover replacement rather than a standalone valve on some service variants.
records.solution: Have the dealer run a documented oil-consumption test; consumption beyond GM's spec can qualify for warranty repair. First-line fix is the PCV/valve-cover assembly (ACDelco PCV service part 12714149 applies to LSY CT5 on standalone-valve variants); persistent consumption after PCV service points to a piston-ring or turbo-seal repair under powertrain warranty. Maintain 5,000-mile changes with dexos1 Gen 3 0W-20 to protect the turbo and rings. Out-of-warranty PCV/valve-cover work is modest; a ring/teardown repair is the expensive end.
symptoms: Frequent low-oil level warnings between oil changes
Burning-oil smell or light blue exhaust smoke
Rough idle or hesitation from a vacuum leak
Check engine light with lean or boost-pressure codes

records.title: 2.0T LSY Engine Timing Cover Oil Leak
records.description: The 2.0T turbocharged four-cylinder (LSY) in the CT5 can develop oil leaks from the timing cover gasket. The gasket develops cracks after heat cycling, causing oil to seep from the front of the engine. In some cases, this leads to noticeable oil consumption between changes. GM revised the 2.0T engine (LSY) for 2020+ which reduced but did not eliminate the issue. Using incorrect oil viscosity can worsen the problem.
records.solution: Confirm the leak by cleaning the front of the LSY engine, adding UV dye if needed, and inspecting the timing cover perimeter, upper oil pan junctions, and front crankshaft seal area to rule out a valve cover or seal leak. Repair typically requires removing the accessory drive components and front cover, resealing or replacing the timing cover gasket/sealant with updated GM parts, and inspecting the cover for warpage or damage before reassembly to factory torque specs; if oil contamination is heavy, replace the drive belt as well. Finish with an oil and filter change using the correct Dexos-approved viscosity specified by GM and verify no further seepage after a road test. Typical repair cost is about $900-$1,800 depending on labor time and whether the front seal, belt, or related seals are replaced.
symptoms: Oil seepage visible at front of engine
Oil spots on garage floor under front of vehicle

records.description:

records.title: Instrument Panel Cluster (IPC / Driver Information Center) Intermittent Blank Screen After Remote Start
records.description: Owners report the digital Instrument Panel Cluster / Driver Information Center (the gauge/speedometer display) going completely blank for the remainder of an ignition cycle, most commonly on cycles that follow a remote start. GM addressed this in Technical Service Bulletin 21-NA-269, which covers the 2020 Cadillac CT4/CT5. The documented root cause is a software fault: infotainment content sent to the IPC from the radio module is sometimes not fully initialized at startup, leaving the cluster blank until the vehicle is shut off and restarted. This is a separate module and separate failure from the center-stack infotainment freezing issue, because it affects the gauge cluster (IPC) and is tied to the startup/remote-start initialization sequence. Verified: the TSB, root cause, and remote-start correlation are corroborated by the GM bulletin summary (oemdtc) and multiple owner reports.
records.solution: Dealer reprograms the Instrument Panel Cluster (IPC) with the latest software calibration per TSB 21-NA-269; no hardware replacement is required in the documented cases. Blank cluster occurs after using remote start
Display stays blank for the entire drive until the car is restarted
No speed, fuel, or warning information shown

records.title: Performance and Carbon-Ceramic Brake Squeal and Grinding Noise
records.description: CT5 and CT5-V owners (and especially CT5-V Blackwing buyers with the optional Brembo carbon-ceramic package) report loud brake squeal, and at low speed a grindy or metal-on-metal sound, sometimes as early as ~5,000 miles. The copper-free friction-material formulation now mandated, combined with the aggressive performance pad compounds, makes the brakes noisy particularly in warm weather and at low speed. This is a comfort/noise issue rather than a stopping-performance defect, but Blackwing carbon-ceramic rotor replacement is extremely expensive if components are damaged.
records.solution: Verify pad and rotor wear and that no wheel cleaner has been used on carbon-ceramic discs (wheel cleaners degrade the carbon fibers). Re-bedding the pads or switching to a quieter aftermarket compound resolves most cases — owners report PowerStop carbon-ceramic pads (Z26-1405 front / 1053 rear-equivalent) eliminate the squeal and reduce dust on iron-rotor cars. Anti-squeal shims/lubricant on pad backing plates help. Avoid spraying any wheel/brake cleaner near carbon-ceramic rotors.
symptoms: Loud brake squeal, worse above ~50F ambient
Squeal when pulling away from a stop

records.title: Premature 12V Battery Drain / Parasitic Draw (Memory Seat Module)
records.description: Owners report the 12V battery going dead when the car sits, with factory batteries dying in as little as two years. Beyond normal high parasitic draw of modern electronics, a recurring GM culprit is the driver-seat control module / Memory Seat Module (MSM), which can develop a several-amp draw that flattens the battery overnight; GM has revised these modules multiple times. Audio/amp circuits, the BCM, and sticking door/window switches are other documented draw sources on GM platforms.
records.solution: Perform a parasitic-draw test: with everything asleep, pull fuses one at a time to isolate the offending circuit. If the seat-control/Memory Seat Module is drawing current, replace it with the latest GM-revised part. Confirm the battery itself still holds charge (replace AGM battery if degraded) and check for sticking door/window switches keeping modules awake. A correct battery and an updated MSM resolve most cases.
symptoms: Dead or weak 12V battery after sitting overnight or a few days

records.title: Upper Intermediate Steering Shaft Chafes Front Brake Line (Service Update N202296840)
records.description:

. 
This chafing can wear through the brake line, causing a loss of brake fluid and reduced braking performance
. Owners may notice no symptoms until brake fluid loss is severe.
records.solution:
Cadillac dealers inspect the front brake lines and replace them if necessary, along with adjacent parts including front lower control arm bolts, various AC compressor seals, and an engine mount bolt; the service bulletin (N202296840, issued January 2021) is performed when the customer vehicle returns to the dealership for any reason and only affects 2020 model year CT5s
. 
The bulletin expires at the end of the New Vehicle Limited Warranty period
. Owners should request the inspection at any service visit and document brake-pedal feel before/after.
symptoms: Visual chafing/wear marks on front brake line near steering shaft
Soft brake pedal if line ruptures
No symptom until severe — often found only on inspection

records.title: Sunroof / Headliner Rattle and Creak

GM has a related sunroof-creak service bulletin (TSB 19-NA-096) that calls for dropping the headliner and torquing the sunroof module bolts to spec. records.solution: For a creak, the dealer follows TSB 19-NA-096 — lower the headliner and re-torque the sunroof bolts to specification. records.title: Super Cruise 'Unavailable' Message — System Inoperative from Delivery
records.description:
Owners report Super Cruise repeatedly displays an 'Unavailable' message and cannot be activated; OnStar troubleshooting fails and dealers escalate to GM engineering with no ETA, citing PIC6557B (Super Cruise Unavailable Message, dated Sept. 25, 2024)

First confirm an active OnStar Super Cruise plan in My Account on Cadillac.com or the mobile app, then verify the road is mapped, system conditions are met, and correct activation steps are followed
. 
Clean the forward camera/radar sensors of dirt and ensure GPS reception; weather and lane-line visibility affect availability

records.title: 10-Speed Transmission Adaptive Learning and Shift Quality
records.description: The CT5 uses GM's 10-speed automatic (10L80) that can exhibit harsh shifts, delayed engagement, and shift hunting, particularly when the adaptive learning resets. The 10-speed has very complex shift logic and can take 500+ miles to fully adapt to a driver's pattern after a battery disconnect, TCM update, or reset. Some CT5 owners report persistent shift quality issues even after adaptation. The CT5-V and CT5-V Blackwing have refined calibrations but can still exhibit occasional harsh shifts.
records.solution: Have dealer perform latest TCM software calibration - GM releases regular updates. Allow 500+ miles after any reset for the transmission to relearn. For persistent issues, a full transmission fluid exchange with Mobil 1 LV ATF HP can improve shift quality. Very few CT5s require hardware repair.

Transmission hunting between gears on hills
Shift quality changes after battery disconnect or service

records.description: The blend door actuator motor fails, causing the HVAC system to blow only hot or only cold air regardless of the temperature setting. records.title: Northstar 4.6L V8 Head Bolt/Head Gasket Failure
records.description: The Cadillac Northstar 4.6L V8 is infamous for head gasket failure caused by the head bolts pulling out of the aluminum engine block. The original design used steel bolts threaded directly into the aluminum block without inserts, and the threads strip over time from heat cycling. This causes coolant to enter the cylinders and exhaust gases to enter the cooling system. The issue typically occurs between 100,000-150,000 miles but can happen earlier. This is one of the most well-known engine failures in automotive history and affects every Northstar-powered Cadillac (DeVille, DTS, Seville, Eldorado). The repair requires engine removal and Time-Sert or Norm's head stud installation.
records.solution: The definitive fix is removing the engine and installing Time-Sert or Norm's Northstar head stud inserts in all head bolt holes, then installing new head gaskets. The head studs clamp the heads properly and prevent the bolts from pulling out of the aluminum block. This repair requires engine removal (the engine comes out the bottom of the car) and is 20-30 hours of labor. Some shops specialize in Northstar head repairs. A "back-yard" chemical head gasket sealer (like Blue Devil) may temporarily slow the leak but is NOT a permanent fix. Prevention: use Dex-Cool coolant and change every 5 years.
symptoms: Coolant loss with no visible external leak
Milky residue on oil cap or dipstick
Bubbles in coolant overflow tank (exhaust gas)

records.title: Northstar 4.6L Engine Oil Leak (Rear Main Seal and Crankcase)

The rear main seal is the most expensive to address as it requires engine removal or separation from the transaxle. The oil leaks have been a known issue since 1998 across all Northstar-equipped models.
symptoms: Burning oil smell from engine bay
Oil visible on lower engine surfaces
Oil on garage floor near rear of engine

citations.title: GM Bulletin 01-06-01-011O - Engine Oil Consumption and Leak-Diagnosis Guidelines

records.title: Northstar 4.6L Head Bolt Thread Pull/Head Gasket Failure
records.description: The Northstar 4.6L V8 in the DTS (and predecessor DeVille) has a well-documented design flaw where the aluminum block head bolt threads strip out, causing head gasket failure. The head gasket itself does not fail; instead the head bolts lose clamping force as the threads pull from the soft aluminum block. The problem is most severe on 1996-2003 engines. GM improved the bolt design in 2000 (longer bolts) and again in 2004 (coarser thread pitch). The Time-Sert thread repair is the accepted permanent fix.
records.solution: Confirm the failure with a block-combustion gas test, cooling-system pressure test, and by checking for repeated overheating/coolant loss with no external leak; on Northstar engines, a positive test usually indicates pulled head-bolt threads rather than a simple gasket defect. The permanent repair is to remove the powertrain, pull both cylinder heads, inspect for warpage/cracks, and install steel thread inserts in all head-bolt holes in the block (Time-Sert is the standard repair; some shops use NS300L/Big-Sert style kits on damaged holes), then reassemble with new head gaskets, new torque-to-yield head bolts, fresh coolant, and related seals. Simply replacing the head gaskets without inserting the block threads will usually fail again. Typical shop cost is about $3,500-$6,500 depending on engine condition and whether additional machine work, inserts, water pump, or crossover/case-half resealing is needed.
symptoms: Overheating with no visible external leak

records.title: Climate Control Head Blank Display and Unresponsive Buttons

records.description: The dual crankshaft position sensors on the 2000-2002 Northstar (which feed the coil-on-plug PCM directly) develop cracked solder joints at an internal resistor, causing intermittent chuggle, stalling while driving, long cranking, or a hot no-start that often resolves once the engine cools. Tachometer drops to zero just before the stall

records.title: Electronic Level Control (ELC) Compressor and Air Shock Failure Causing Rear Sag
records.description: The Eldorado's self-leveling rear suspension uses an electric air compressor, height sensor, and air-adjustable rear shocks. Aging air shocks and lines develop leaks that force the compressor to run constantly until its internal dryer clogs with moisture and the pump burns out or seizes, leaving the rear end sagging. RepairPal documents the auto level ride compressor as a known Eldorado failure, and forum diagnostic threads consistently stress that leaks must be fixed first or the replacement pump will die the same way.
records.solution: Find and repair air leaks first (shocks and lines are the usual culprits), then replace the compressor and dryer if the pump no longer builds pressure. Many owners replace the worn air shocks at the same time; budget roughly $250-$900 at an independent shop depending on how many components are replaced.
symptoms: Rear end sits noticeably low, especially with passengers or trunk cargo
Compressor hum behind the rear seat runs constantly or never runs at all
Bouncy, wallowing, or harsh rear ride
Rear suspension bottoms out over bumps when loaded
Vehicle leans or fails to re-level after loading

records.title: Northstar Cold-Start Carbon Knock (Carbon Rap / Piston Slap Noise)
records.description: The Northstar's tight piston-to-head squish clearance lets carbon deposits build up on the piston crowns and combustion chambers, especially in cars driven gently on short trips. When cold, the piston rocks against the carbon and produces a rhythmic rap that sounds alarmingly like rod knock or piston slap but fades as the engine warms. GM addressed it with an induction carbon-cleaning procedure, and in severe persistent cases TSB 03-06-01-025 (covering 2000-2002 Eldorado) authorized piston replacement.
records.solution: Decarbonize the combustion chambers with GM Top Engine Cleaner per the GM service procedure, then perform periodic wide-open-throttle accelerations to keep carbon from re-accumulating. Only rare, severe cases that persist after cleaning warrant the piston replacement described in TSB 03-06-01-025.
symptoms: Rhythmic knock or rap on cold start that fades as the engine warms
Noise most noticeable after extended short-trip, light-throttle driving
Sounds like piston slap or rod knock when cold, quiet when hot
Noise diminishes after a few hard wide-open-throttle accelerations

records.title: Northstar 4.6L V8 Head Bolt/Head Gasket Failure
records.description: The 1993-2002 Eldorado was one of the first vehicles to receive the Northstar 4.6L V8 and has the same head bolt/head gasket failure. Early Northstar engines (1993-1995) are particularly prone as the design was less refined. The Eldorado ETC (Touring Coupe) uses the high-output 300hp Northstar. Same failure mechanism and repair as all Northstar-powered Cadillacs.
records.solution: Engine removal and head stud/Time-Sert installation. Given the age and value of Eldorados, many owners must weigh repair cost ($3-6k) against vehicle value. Eldorado enthusiasts still perform the repair for collector vehicles.
symptoms: Coolant loss with no visible external leak

records.title: Northstar V8 Chronic Oil Leaks (Rear Main Seal and Lower Crankcase Half-Case Seal)
records.description: Beyond its famous head gasket woes, the Northstar 4.6L V8 is notorious for external oil leaks from its two-piece crankcase design. The block is split into upper and lower halves sealed with anaerobic sealant, and as the engine ages this case-half seal, the rear main seal, valve cover gaskets, and oil pan seal all weep or drip. Rear main seal oil drips directly onto the hot exhaust crossover pipe, causing burning-oil odors, and case-half leaks require engine removal to repair properly on the transverse Eldorado.
records.solution: Minor leaks (valve covers, oil pressure sensor) are inexpensive gasket jobs; rear main seal replacement runs roughly $600-$800. A leaking lower crankcase half-case seal requires pulling the engine and resealing, commonly quoted at $2,000-$2,500, so many shops recommend a comprehensive reseal of all seals while the engine is out.
symptoms: Oil spots on the driveway after parking
Burning-oil smell from the exhaust crossover area after driving
Oil film coating the lower engine, pan rails, and bellhousing
Oil level drops between changes with no visible exhaust smoke
Drips concentrated at the rear of the engine near the transaxle

records.title: Water Pump Drive Belt and Tensioner Pulley Failure Causing Sudden Overheating
records.description: The Northstar drives its water pump off the intake camshaft with a short dedicated belt and spring tensioner behind a cover at the rear of the engine, separate from the main accessory belt. The tensioner pulley bearing dries out and seizes or disintegrates with age, which shreds the belt and can melt the plastic cam-driven pulley, instantly stopping all coolant circulation. Because a Northstar that is driven while overheating quickly cooks its head gaskets, a $25 pulley can become a multi-thousand-dollar engine job if the temperature warning is ignored.
records.solution: Replace the water pump drive belt and tensioner pulley (and the cam-driven pulley if it melted); many owners replace the tensioner preventively around 75,000-100,000 miles since parts are cheap and access is straightforward. Stop driving immediately at any sign of overheating to protect the head gaskets.

Squeal, chirp, or rattle from the water pump belt cover at the rear of the engine

records.title: "Shift to Park" False Warning from Failing Electronic Shifter Park Switch
records.description: The ELR uses an electronic precision shift lever that springs back to a center rest position and relies on an internal park-detent microswitch to confirm the transmission is in Park. On the ELR this internal park switch degrades and intermittently fails to send the 'in Park' signal, producing a persistent 'Shift to Park' warning even though the lever is already in Park, which prevents the driver from powering the car down. The fault is intermittent (can occur several times a day, then disappear for a week), which is characteristic of a worn switch contact rather than a software glitch. When it occurs, the car may repeatedly chime and stay awake until it times out (owners report roughly 20 minutes), and repeated occurrences can contribute to 12V battery drain. Owners on the Cadillac and GM-Volt forums document the identical symptom, and the same GM electronic-shifter 'Shift to Park' condition became the subject of a nationwide class-action lawsuit.
records.solution: Temporary workaround owners report: lightly pull the lever out of the Park detent and release, or flick the small silver override switch on the back of the shifter, which forces the car into shutdown. The accepted permanent repair is replacement of the electronic precision shift lever/console shifter assembly; owners report the part costs over $200 and total dealer repair around $548. If the shifter left systems awake and drained the 12V battery, it may need recharging or replacement at the same time.
symptoms: 'Shift to Park' message displayed even though the lever is in Park

Possible 12V battery drain from systems staying awake

records.title: Sudden Total Loss of Electrical Power While Driving (Often With No Stored Codes)
records.description: Multiple ELR owners report a frightening intermittent failure in which the car loses ALL electrical power without warning while driving - sometimes preceded by a loud 'pop' - taking out power steering, power brake assist, lights, hazard flashers, gauges and even door locks, forcing the driver to wrestle the car to the shoulder. A defining (and maddening) trait is that the car frequently restarts normally after towing and leaves no diagnostic trouble codes, so dealers struggle to reproduce or diagnose it. Suspected sources include the 12V system/grounds, the high-voltage contactor/relay in the battery, or the battery energy control module, but root cause is often not confirmed.
records.solution: Treat as a safety-priority intermittent electrical fault. Start with a thorough 12V battery, charging and ground-circuit inspection (a weak or marginal 12V auxiliary system is a common trigger on Voltec cars), then have a Voltec-certified tech inspect the HV battery disconnect/contactors and high-current connections for arcing or loose terminals (consistent with the reported 'pop'). Capture freeze-frame/history data immediately after an event before clearing anything, and document each occurrence for GM, since the lack of stored codes makes a contemporaneous log the best diagnostic lever. Costs range from a cheap ground/terminal repair to HV contactor or module replacement.
symptoms: Loud 'pop' before power loss in some cases
Loss of power steering and power brake assist
Dash, lights, flashers and door locks all dead
Car restarts normally later with no fault codes

records.description: The Escalade AWD system uses a transfer case (NP149 full-time AWD or NP246 selectable 4WD on ESV models) that commonly experiences encoder motor failure and internal chain stretch. The encoder motor controls the transfer case mode selection and wears out between 80,000-130,000 miles. Symptoms include grinding noises when shifting between 2WD/4WD, SERVICE 4WD messages, and the system defaulting to 2WD. Internal chain stretch can cause a whining noise and eventual failure. Transfer case fluid changes are often neglected, accelerating wear.
records.solution: Diagnose the specific failure. The encoder motor (shift motor) is the most common failure and can be replaced independently for $300-600. Internal chain stretch requires transfer case rebuild or replacement. Regular transfer case fluid changes every 50,000 miles with Auto-Trak II fluid (NP149) or Dexron VI (NP246) can prevent premature wear. Some owners upgrade to a Merchant Automotive encoder motor for improved longevity.
symptoms: SERVICE 4WD or SERVICE AWD message on dash
Grinding noise when shifting transfer case modes
Whining noise from under vehicle at highway speed
Transfer case stuck in one mode
Vibration at 40-60 mph that comes and goes

records.title: Cooling System and Heater Core Failure
records.description: The Fleetwood (both 5.7L TBI and LT1 versions) develops cooling system issues including water pump failure, heater core leaks, and radiator degradation. The heater core replacement requires extensive dash removal.

After repairs, flush the system, refill with the correct 50/50 coolant mix, bleed air, verify fan operation and operating temperature, and replace aged hoses, belt, and radiator cap if original. Typical costs are about $400-$900 for a water pump job, $500-$1,000 for a radiator, and roughly $1,000-$1,800 for a heater core due to labor intensity.

records.title: Inconsistent DC Fast-Charging Speed With Mid-Session Power Dips
records.description: Independent testing (including Tom Moloughney / InsideEVs) and owner-logged curves show the Lyriq peaks near 188-190 kW on a healthy 150-350 kW DC fast charger but suffers abrupt power plunges mid-session (notably around 52% and again near 77-80% state of charge), dragging the 10-80% average down to roughly 90-130 kW. The 400-volt architecture means a 350 kW charger gives no advantage over a 150 kW unit, so fast-charge stops take longer than the headline rate suggests.
records.solution: Precondition the battery before a DC fast-charge stop to reach and hold higher rates. Much of the behavior is inherent to the Lyriq's charge curve, but keep the vehicle software current (GM has tuned thermal/charging logic via OTA updates), choose an uncongested high-power charger, and report persistently abnormal low rates to a dealer to rule out a thermal-management fault.

records.title: Northstar 4.6L Head Gasket Failure
records.description: The Northstar V8 in the Seville shares the same head gasket failure as all Northstar-equipped vehicles. records.solution: The industry-standard repair uses Time-Sert inserts to repair the head bolt threads in the aluminum block with stronger steel threads. records.title: 4.6L Northstar V8 Head Gasket Failure and Bolt Pull-Out
records.description: The Northstar V8 in the STS is infamous for head gasket failure caused by the head bolts pulling out of the aluminum block. GM used torque-to-yield head bolts threaded directly into the aluminum block without steel inserts, and over time the bolt threads strip from the soft aluminum. Coolant enters the combustion chambers, causing overheating and white exhaust smoke. This issue affects virtually every high-mileage Northstar engine and is often terminal for the vehicle due to repair costs exceeding vehicle value.
records.solution: The permanent fix is the Northstar Performance "Norm's Inserts" or Time-Sert procedure — the engine is removed, heads pulled, and steel thread inserts are installed in all head bolt locations in the aluminum block. This is a 30+ hour job. Alternatively, a used/reman engine with inserts already installed can be swapped in. Bar's Leaks Head Gasket Fix (1111) is a temporary measure that can buy time.

If caught early, a body shop can weld reinforcement plates. If advanced, the mounts may need to be cut out and new mounting plates welded in. This is a structural repair that must be done properly for safety.

records.title: 2.0T LSY Engine - PCV and Turbo Coolant Line Issues
records.description: The XT4 uses the 2.0T LSY engine which is an evolution of the LTG found in the ATS/CTS. The turbo coolant lines can develop leaks at the connections, causing coolant loss and potential turbo damage from overheating. The PCV valve/cover can fail causing oil consumption. These issues typically appear between 40,000-80,000 miles.
records.solution: Inspect turbo coolant lines and connections for leaks - replace lines if seeping. PCV system is integrated into valve cover - replace valve cover assembly if PCV fails. records.title: 2.0L Turbo Excessive Oil Consumption

records.solution: Monitor oil level between changes and top off as needed. Use only Dexos1 Gen3 certified 0W-20 synthetic oil. Have the PCV system inspected for proper function. If consumption exceeds 1 quart per 2,000 miles, request a GM oil consumption test from the dealer. Document consumption for warranty purposes.

records.title: Front Brake Rotor Warping and Pedal Pulsation
records.description: The front brake rotors warp prematurely, causing steering wheel vibration and brake pedal pulsation during moderate to hard braking. The issue is attributed to the heavy vehicle weight combined with rotors that are borderline in thickness for the application. Aggressive braking or mountain driving accelerates warping.
records.solution: Replace the front brake rotors with quality aftermarket rotors that meet or exceed OEM thickness. Bed in the new rotors and pads properly with a series of moderate stops. Avoid hard braking followed by holding the brake (which creates hot spots). Upgrading to slotted rotors can help manage heat better.
symptoms: Vibration worse at highway speed braking

records.title: Electronic Gear Selector Park-Switch Fault - Persistent 'Shift to Park' Message / Won't Power Down (TSB 19-NA-206)
records.description: A faulty park-position switch inside the electronic shifter assembly intermittently fails to signal that the vehicle is in Park. This produces a persistent 'Shift to Park' message on the driver information center even when the lever is physically in Park, and the vehicle may refuse to fully power down, staying in accessory mode and draining the 12V battery overnight. Owners report shifter codes such as P07BE and P26C8. GM addressed the concern with TSB 19-NA-206. This is an electronic-shifter/electrical failure, separate from internal transmission shudder/harsh-shift issues.
records.solution: Per GM TSB 19-NA-206 the repair is often installing an in-line jumper harness (P/N 84733196) at the shifter connector; where that does not resolve it, the shifter assembly is replaced. Replacement requires removing the center console trim and generally needs no special programming. Pressing the Park button squarely in the center can be a temporary workaround for the dual-sensor design.
symptoms: 'Shift to Park' message stays on with lever already in Park
Vehicle will not fully shut off / stays in accessory mode
Dead 12V battery overnight from failure to power down
Intermittent refusal to shift out of Park

records.title: Power Liftgate Strut Failure and Erratic Operation
records.description: The power liftgate struts lose their charge and fail to hold the liftgate open, causing it to slowly close or fall. records.solution: Replace both power liftgate struts as a pair. Use OEM struts for proper fit with the power liftgate system. After replacement, the liftgate height setting may need to be reprogrammed. If the liftgate motor is also weak, it should be replaced at the same time. records.title: 3.6L V6 Timing Chain Issues (XT5 V6 models)
records.description: The XT5 V6 models use the GM 3.6L V6 (LGX) which has improved timing chains over earlier versions but is not immune to timing chain stretch at higher mileage. The LGX is better than the earlier LFX but still uses three timing chains with plastic guides. Issues typically appear later (100,000-150,000 miles) compared to earlier 3.6L variants. The 2020+ XT5 2.0T models use a different engine (LSY) and are not affected by this issue.
records.solution: Same timing chain replacement as SRX/CTS 3.6L. Cloyes 9-0753S kit, replace water pump simultaneously. The LGX timing chain typically lasts longer than the LFX, so preventive replacement at 100,000+ miles is recommended rather than the 80,000-mile interval for earlier engines.

records.title: 8-Speed / 9-Speed Transmission Shudder and Harsh Shifting

records.title: Auto Start-Stop Harshness and Battery Issues
records.description: The auto start-stop system engages and disengages harshly, causing the vehicle to shudder on restart. The AGM battery required for the system degrades quickly, and when it weakens, the start-stop system becomes erratic or disables itself. Many owners find the system intrusive.
records.solution: Replace the AGM battery with a fresh ACDelco unit if the system is not functioning properly. Have the battery monitor sensor reset after replacement. GM has released recalibrations to improve start-stop smoothness. Aftermarket start-stop eliminator modules are available for owners who want to permanently disable the feature.

records.title: AWD Power Transfer Unit Fluid Leak
records.description: The Power Transfer Unit (PTU) on AWD-equipped XT6 models develops seal leaks that allow fluid to seep out. Low PTU fluid causes the internal gears and bearings to wear prematurely, eventually producing a whining noise. The PTU is not included in routine maintenance schedules, so leaks often go unnoticed.
records.solution: Inspect the PTU seals and replace if leaking. Top off with the GM-specified PTU fluid. If the PTU is already noisy from running low on fluid, replacement is required as the unit is not rebuildable. Add PTU fluid level check to your routine maintenance schedule every 15,000 miles.
symptoms: Fluid leak near front of transmission

records.title: 3.6L V6 Timing Chain Concern (XT6)
records.description: The XT6 uses the GM 3.6L V6 (LGX) which has a documented history of timing chain stretch across the GM lineup. While the LGX generation is improved over earlier 3.6L variants, the three-chain design with plastic guides remains a long-term reliability concern. Most XT6s are still too new for widespread timing chain failures, but owners should monitor for early signs and plan for preventive replacement around 100,000-120,000 miles based on the engine's history in other models.
records.solution: Monitor for timing chain rattle on cold starts. If codes or rattle develop, complete timing chain replacement is needed. Preventive replacement at 100,000-120,000 miles is wise based on the 3.6L's track record. Same Cloyes 9-0753S kit as other 3.6L applications.
symptoms: Rattling on cold start that goes away when warm
Check engine light with timing correlation codes at higher mileage

records.title: 9-Speed Automatic Transmission Shudder and Harsh Shifts
records.description: The XT6's GM 9T65 9-speed automatic transmission exhibits shuddering during light throttle acceleration between 25-50 mph, similar to driving over rumble strips. The torque converter clutch wears prematurely, contaminating the transmission fluid.
records.solution: A transmission fluid flush with the updated Mobil 1 Blue Label fluid resolves mild cases. Severe cases require torque converter replacement. A GM TSB authorizes fluid flush as the first repair attempt.
symptoms: Feels like driving over rumble strips
Shudder worse when transmission is warm

records.title: 3.6L Direct-Injection Intake Valve Carbon Buildup
records.description: The 3.6L V6 (LFX naturally-aspirated and LF3 twin-turbo) uses direct fuel injection, so no fuel washes over the backs of the intake valves. Combined with a PCV system that routes oil vapor into the intake tract, carbon coking accumulates on the intake valves over time. By roughly 60,000-100,000 miles this can cause rough idle, misfires, hesitation, and reduced fuel economy/power. This is separate from timing-chain-stretch and high-pressure fuel-pump issues; it is a fueling/airflow deposit problem inherent to GDI engines.
records.solution: Clean the intake valves by walnut-shell media blasting (the accepted fix for GDI coking); chemical intake cleaners help mildly but do not remove hardened deposits. To slow recurrence, install an oil catch can on the PCV line and/or a reduced-orifice PCV to keep oil vapor out of the intake. Periodic top-end cleaning is preventive maintenance on these DI engines.
symptoms: Check engine light with misfire codes

records.title: HID Xenon Headlight Ballast Failure & Housing Moisture
records.description: XTS HID/Xenon headlamps suffer ballast (HID control unit) failures and headlight-housing condensation that cause intermittent or total loss of a low beam. Owners report flickering, a headlamp that cuts out then comes back, or a dead side after a new bulb. Moisture entering the housing is a frequent root cause — water reaching the ballast causes rapid failure — and corrosion in the headlight wiring/ground (often shared with the upper LED DRL) can take out both the ballast and DRL together.
records.solution: Diagnose by swapping the D3S bulb side-to-side; if the fault follows the position, the ballast/igniter is bad, not the bulb. Replace the failed HID ballast/control module and reseal the housing; dry out and re-gasket any housing showing condensation. Inspect the ballast connector and chassis ground for corrosion and repair before installing new parts, or the new ballast will fail again. Use OEM-grade D3S bulbs and a matching ballast to avoid color/flicker issues.

New bulb still doesn't fix it

records.title: High-Pressure Direct-Injection Fuel Pump Failure
records.description: The engine-mounted high-pressure fuel pump (HPFP) on the GM 3.6L direct-injection V6 is a known wear item that fails on the XTS, causing long crank/no-start (especially warm restart), rough idle, stalling and misfires. The most common codes are P0087 (fuel rail pressure too low), P0089 (fuel pressure regulator performance) and P0191 (rail pressure sensor), often with random misfire P0300. Because the high-pressure pump is cam-driven off the engine, a failing pump can drive adaptive fuel trims that mask early symptoms until it strands the car.
records.solution: Perform a live high-side fuel-pressure test during acceleration and on a warm restart to confirm the HPFP versus injectors or the low-pressure (in-tank) pump. Replace the high-pressure fuel pump and its sealing/lifter components; many shops also replace the camshaft pump-drive lifter and inspect the lobe. Use fresh GM-spec fuel-system sealant and torque to spec to avoid leaks. OEM HPFP PN 12641740 (supersedes 12622475; aftermarket Delphi HM10007 / GDP106 cross-references). Reset fuel trims after the repair.
symptoms: Extended crank or no-start, worse when warm

records.title: HVAC Blend Door Actuator Clicking / Blower Resistor No Heat
records.description: Two related HVAC complaints are common on the XTS: a repetitive clicking/knocking from behind the dash caused by a failing blend-door (temperature) actuator that can't reach its calibration stop, and loss of fan-speed control or no heat from a failed blower motor resistor/module — when the resistor fails the fan often works only on the highest setting. Owners report inconsistent temperature (one side hot/one cold) with the actuator fault and a dead or single-speed blower with the resistor fault.
records.solution: For the clicking: identify the failing blend-door actuator (listen/feel behind the dash while cycling temperature), replace the actuator and re-run the HVAC calibration/relearn. For no/limited fan: test the blower motor resistor/control module and the blower motor itself; replace the failed resistor module (and motor if it's drawing high current). Clear any HVAC actuator codes after replacement.
symptoms: One side blows hot, other cold
Blower only works on high speed
No fan / no air from vents
No heat or no cold air

records.title: Parasitic Battery Drain / Modules Not Entering Sleep Mode
records.description: XTS owners frequently report the 12V battery going dead overnight or after a few days of sitting, caused by a control module failing to enter sleep mode and continuing to draw current with the ignition off. Common culprits on this platform include the radio/CUE (infotainment) module and the BCM. Repeated deep discharges then prematurely kill the battery and can trigger low-state-of-charge warnings and start-stop faults. GM issued service information for low-battery-state-of-charge conditions on 2018-2019 XTS/ATS/CTS.
records.solution: Perform a parasitic-draw test (normal is under ~50mA once modules sleep, roughly 30-40 seconds after lockup) and pull-fuse isolation to find the circuit that stays awake. Common fixes include replacing/reflashing a faulty CUE/radio module or BCM, repairing a chattering switch/connector that wakes the bus, and removing non-OEM accessories (aftermarket LEDs are a documented trigger). Replace the battery if it has been repeatedly deep-cycled.
symptoms: Battery dead after sitting overnight or a few days
Low battery / reduced electrical features warnings

records.title: Passenger Presence System Fault / Passenger Airbag Light On
records.description: The front passenger seat contains a Passenger Presence System (occupant-classification sensor/module and wiring harness) that tells the airbag controller whether to enable the passenger airbag. On the XTS the sensor mat, the under-seat connector, and the wiring harness are prone to faults, illuminating the SRS/'Service Air Bag' warning and often leaving the PASSENGER AIRBAG OFF indicator stuck on (or incorrectly on with an adult seated). Because a fault can disable passenger airbag deployment, this is a genuine safety concern.
records.solution: Diagnose with a scan tool for airbag/occupant-classification codes. First inspect, reseat, and clean the under-seat connector and wiring harness (corroded/loose pins are the most common cause). If the sensor/pressure-mat or Passenger Presence Module itself has failed, replace it; in some cases the sensor is integrated into the seat cushion, raising cost. A post-repair occupant-classification recalibration may be required.
symptoms: Service Air Bag / SRS warning light
Passenger airbag indicator stuck OFF with adult seated
Airbag light on after seat work

records.title: Rear Air Suspension Sudden Collapse (F38 Air Ride)
records.description: XTS models equipped with the optional rear air-leveling suspension (RPO F38) suffer sudden, total collapse of the rear air springs/struts, often without warning and sometimes at highway speed. NHTSA/CarComplaints reports describe the rear dropping so low the tires nearly contact the wheel wells, causing the rear end to bounce and loss of vehicle control. Root causes include failed rear air springs (perforation/dry-rot), a worn-out air dryer/desiccant that lets moisture accumulate, and air compressor/air-line failures. A 'Service Leveling System' message and the car sitting low or unlevel are the early warning signs. The 2013 model year alone shows ~24 logged suspension complaints, the highest-volume XTS problem after CUE.
records.solution: Diagnose with a scan tool for leveling-system codes and a smoke/soap test of the air springs and lines. Replace failed rear air springs/struts and the air supply unit (compressor with integrated dryer). Many owners with repeat failures convert to a passive coil-spring/strut conversion kit (Strutmasters/Arnott) to permanently eliminate the air system. Always replace the air dryer/desiccant when servicing the compressor or moisture will quickly kill the new unit. OEM compressor assembly PN 84355910 (ACDelco 22956965); Arnott aftermarket compressor and spring kits are common cross-references.
symptoms: Rear end suddenly drops/sags, tires near wheel wells
Car sits low or unlevel at rest
Air compressor runs constantly or not at all
Rear bouncing / loss of control over bumps

records.title: Safety Alert Seat Haptic Motor Failure
records.description: The Safety Alert Seat uses haptic (vibration) motors in the left and right seat bolsters to pulse warnings for lane departure, blind spot, and forward collision. One side commonly stops vibrating (left or right only), or the system randomly switches between vibrate and chime. The documented weak point is a wire breaking where it enters the haptic motor assembly. Because GM ties this hardware into the driver-assist suite, a failed seat motor frequently also triggers a 'Service Driver Assist System' message.
records.solution: Confirm the dead side by triggering lane-departure to each side; if only one bolster pulses, the opposite motor/wire has failed. Replace the affected seat haptic vibration motor (left or right bumper-alert motor) and repair the broken wire at the motor entry. If the seat hardware checks out, scan the BCM for driver-assist codes and update software, since a glitch can mimic the failure. As a stopgap, owners can switch Alert Type to 'beeps' in the menu to restore audible warnings.
symptoms: No vibration on one side of seat
Seat randomly switches to chime instead of buzz
Lane-departure/blind-spot light flashes but no buzz

records.title: Sunroof Drain Leak / Headliner Water Damage
records.description: The XTS dual-panel sunroof is prone to water intrusion that stains the cloth headliner and wets the front/rear passenger footwells. The design uses the same perimeter seal on the fixed glass as the moving panel (doubling leak-off) with undersized drain tubes that clog easily with debris, overwhelming the system in heavy rain. The problem became significant enough that Cadillac faced a class-action lawsuit over leaking sunroofs across several models. Water can also reach electrical modules under the carpet, causing secondary electrical faults.
records.solution: Flush all four sunroof drain tubes with low-pressure compressed air or a flexible trimmer line (avoid stiff wire that can pop the hose off at the bottom). Verify water exits at the rocker/A-pillar and rear quarter outlets. Replace cracked/age-hardened sunroof perimeter gaskets and reseat the drain hose grommets; in stubborn cases seal the leaking drain-tube connection. Dry and replace stained headliner/insulation and check for wet carpet over body control modules.
symptoms: Water dripping onto headliner or A-pillar
Wet front or rear floor carpet

records.title: Multiple Cam/Crank Correlation DTCs Require Chain, Tensioner and Reluctor Diagnosis
records.description: GM PIP3423P covers 2013-2019 XTS vehicles with the 3.6L LFX or LF3 engine when two or more of P0008, P0009 and P0016-P0019 are present. GM directs technicians to check for loose chains or tensioners and, if normal SI diagnosis does not find the cause, inspect whether the crankshaft-sensor reluctor moved. The bulletin does not establish automatic chain replacement.
records.solution: Have a qualified technician confirm that at least two listed correlation DTCs are present, then follow current SI diagnosis for chains and tensioners. If the cause remains unresolved, inspect the crankshaft reluctor as directed by PIP3423P. Do not order the former generic timing kit or water pump from this card; the exact ShowMeTheParts lookup returned no timing-chain candidate.
symptoms: Check-engine light with two or more correlation DTCs

records.title: Launch or 2-3/3-2 Shift Shudder Must Be Separated from TCC Shudder
records.description: GM bulletin 18-NA-358 covers 2014-2019 XTS vehicles with 6T70, 6T75 or 6T80 transmissions RPO M7U, M7W, M7V or MHM when severe launch or fourth-gear shudder, a 2-3 upshift or 3-2 downshift concern, flare, slip or harsh shift is present. Debris or scoring in the upper or lower valve body may be involved, but GM first requires ruling out engine driveability and torque-converter clutch shudder.
records.solution: Have a qualified transmission technician verify the transmission RPO, reproduce the exact event and monitor TCC slip. Do not replace the TEHCM for this symptom. If diagnosis confirms the bulletin valve-body condition, follow current SI for both upper and lower valve-body replacement. Do not use a universal fluid or additive; the exact ShowMeTheParts lookup returned no transmission-fluid candidate.
symptoms: Severe shudder during launch in first gear
Flare, slide/bump, slip or harsh shift
affectedSystems: upper and lower control valve bodies

records.title: Water Pump Weep-Hole Coolant Leak (3.6L V6)
records.description: The 3.6L V6 water pump develops an internal seal failure that lets coolant seep from the pump's weep hole — a designed indicator that the pump's internal shaft seal has failed. Owners commonly mistake the weep-hole drip for a 'pinhole' and try stop-leak, but it signals the pump is failing internally and will progress to overheating and potential head-gasket/engine damage. Low-coolant warnings, sweet smell, and white residue at the front of the engine are typical. RepairPal lists coolant leaks (pump, hoses, radiator) among the most common XTS cooling complaints.
records.solution: Confirm the source: clean the area and look for fresh coolant tracking from the weep hole below the water pump pulley (versus hose clamps or the radiator). Replace the water pump with a new OEM/ACDelco unit and gasket, refill with DEX-COOL, and pressure-test. Do NOT use stop-leak — it can clog the heater core and radiator. ACDelco Gold water pump PN 19325605 (aftermarket ACDelco 252-962 cross-reference); inspect the thermostat and upper/lower hoses while the system is open.
symptoms: Coolant dripping from weep hole / front of engine
White or orange crust on water pump
